paper.title: Algorithm 454: The complex method for constrained optimization (JCONSX)
paper.venue: Communications of the ACM 16(8), August 1973, pp. 487-489 (archive header: COLLECTED ALGORITHMS FROM ACM, VOL. 16, NO. 8, August 1973, PP. 487-489)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 454.gz (scouted 2026-11-27, gz sha256 62edf4cce130c6e7ccce05b9da7908b3446ac74ce5ae74ca1fe9fe80087cf9f0). A shell archive (#! /bin/sh, created 10 March 2006 by J. Burkardt's packaging) of Fortran/Sp/Src/src.f (JCONSX), Fortran/Sp/Drivers/driver1.f, driver2.f, driver3.f, a Makefile and the reference files res1, res2, res3 that the Makefile diffs against.

claim.location: Fortran/Sp/Drivers/res1, the shipped reference output of driver1.f (TOMS454_PRB1, the Box problem). Its last printed iterate before the exact-solution line is ITERATION 20, CORRECTED POINT 3.0000 1.7320, and the run then prints ITERATION 21 and 'The exact solution is F(3.0000,1.7321)'. driver1.f sets seed = 123456789 at line 71 and fills the starting points with the Park-Miller generator RN. The rerun should compile src.f and driver1.f unedited and compare the ITERATION 20 corrected point and the ITERATION 21 count with res1.

reference.file: 454.gz, extracted Fortran/Sp/Drivers/res1 (produced by the archive's own driver, shipped in the shar)
reference.sha256: not recorded for the extracted res1; the archive sha256 is 62edf4cce130c6e7ccce05b9da7908b3446ac74ce5ae74ca1fe9fe80087cf9f0

claim.metric: Corrected point of the complex method on the Box problem (driver1, seeded starting points) at ITERATION 20: the two coordinates printed to four decimals, and the number of iterations printed before the exact-solution line (21).
claim.paper_value: Not checked against the paper (CACM 16(8) 487-489 is behind the ACM paywall); the archive's shipped res1 is the value to check.

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. res1 prints the coordinates to four decimals, so the print rounding is up to 5e-5 per coordinate; 6e-5 absorbs it and nothing more. The iteration count is an integer and must match exactly. A different compiler or libm may move the last bits, and the Park-Miller generator is integer, so this is the deterministic check. Not loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 second (21 iterations of a 2-variable problem).
cost.data_size: Archive 454.gz is a 2774-line shar; no data files.
cost.data_licence: Not stated in the archive; a Collected Algorithm from ACM. The rerun should record the licence it finds.

why: The shipped driver and reference res1 print a seeded, deterministic run of JCONSX's complex method that converges to the known Box-problem optimum, so the iterate path and the convergence count are checked without any paper table.
